Class SubListAdapterTest

java.lang.Object
myTest.SubListAdapterTest
public class SubListAdapterTest extends Object
Test suite for the SubListAdapter class.

This test suite verifies the functionality of the SubListAdapter class, which provides a view of a portion of a VectorAdapter or another SubListAdapter. The tests cover various scenarios including normal usage, element access, modification, collection access and modification, edge cases and error conditions.

Test Case Design

The test cases are designed to validate the behavior of SubListAdapter against the specifications of Java 1.4.2 Vector class subList functionality. The test design includes categories for basic functionality, edge cases, error conditions, and interaction with the backing vector.

Testing Framework Information

This test suite utilizes JUnit 4.13 testing framework with Hamcrest 1.3 matchers for assertions. These dependencies are located as follows:

  • JUnit 4.13: lib/junit-4.13.jar
  • Hamcrest Core 1.3: Matcher/hamcrest-core-1.3.jar

Categories:

  • Constructor and initialization tests
  • Basic functionality tests
  • Element access and modification tests
  • Size and capacity management tests
  • Collection operation tests
  • Iterator functionality tests
  • Edge case and exception handling tests

      public void setUp()
      Sets up the testing environment before each test method execution. Initializes the vector and subList instances to null to ensure the use of a clean state.

    • testSubListValidParameters

      public void testSubListValidParameters()
      Test method to verify that subList creation works correctly with valid parameters.

      Summary:

      This test verifies that a sublist can be created with valid indices and contains the correct elements.

      Test Case Design:

      The test validates basic sublist functionality with normal parameters, ensuring proper element selection and size calculation.

      Test Description:

      The test creates a VectorAdapter with 5 elements, then creates a sublist from indices 1 to 4. It verifies that the sublist contains the correct elements at the expected positions and has the correct size.

      Pre-Condition:

      - VectorAdapter is initialized with 5 elements: ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5"]

      Post-Condition:

      - SubListAdapter is successfully created with size 3

      - Sublist contains elements ["2", "3", "4"]

      Expected Results:

      Sublist should be created successfully with correct elements and size.

    • testSubListSingleElement

      public void testSubListSingleElement()
      Test method to verify that subList creation works correctly for a single element range.

      Summary:

      This test verifies that a single-element sublist is properly created.

      Test Case Design:

      The test validates sublist functionality for the edge case of a single element range.

      Test Description:

      The test creates a VectorAdapter with 3 elements, then creates a sublist from indices 1 to 2. It verifies that the sublist contains exactly one element at position 0.

      Pre-Condition:

      - VectorAdapter is initialized with 3 elements: ["1", "2", "3"]

      Post-Condition:

      - SubListAdapter is successfully created with size 1

      - Sublist contains element "2" at index 0

      Expected Results:

      Sublist should be created successfully with one correct element.

      Post-Condition:

    • testSubListFullRange

      public void testSubListFullRange()
      Test method to verify that subList creation works correctly for a full range.

      Summary:

      This test verifies that a sublist covering the entire vector can be created correctly.

      Test Case Design:

      The test validates sublist functionality for the case of a full range selection.

      Test Description:

      The test creates a VectorAdapter with 3 elements, then creates a sublist from indices 0 to 3. It verifies that the sublist contains all elements in the correct order.

      Pre-Condition:

      - VectorAdapter is initialized with 3 elements: ["1", "2", "3"]

      Post-Condition:

      - SubListAdapter is successfully created with size 3

      - Sublist contains all original elements in order

      Expected Results:

      Full-range sublist should be created successfully with all elements preserved.

    • testSubListNullElements

      This test verifies that a sublist containing null elements can be created and handled correctly.

      Test Case Design:

      The test validates sublist functionality with null values, ensuring proper handling of null elements.

      Test Description:

      The test creates a VectorAdapter with 4 null elements, then creates a sublist from indices 1 to 3. It verifies that the sublist contains the correct number of null elements.

      public void testSubListConstructorFromIndexGreaterThanToIndex()
      Test method to verify that subList constructor throws IllegalArgumentException when fromIndex bigger than toIndex.

      Summary:

      This test verifies proper exception handling for invalid index.

      Test Case Design:

      The test validates exception handling for the edge case of fromIndex bigger than toIndex.

      Test Description:

      The test attempts to create a sublist with fromIndex 2 and toIndex 1, expecting an IllegalArgumentException to be thrown.

      Pre-Condition:

      - VectorAdapter is initialized with 2 elements: ["1", "2"]

      Post-Condition:

      - No sublist is created

      Expected Results:

      IllegalArgumentException should be thrown when fromIndex bigger than toIndex.

      public void testSubListToStringWithOffset()
      Test method to verify the string representation of a sublist with offset positioning.

      Summary:

      This test verifies that a sublist with offset positioning within its backing vector produces the correct string representation.

      Test Case Design:

      The test validates that the toString() correctly represents sublists that start at an offset position within their backing vectors.

      Test Description:

      The test creates a VectorAdapter with five elements, creates a sublist starting at index 2, and verifies its string representation matches the expected format for the subset of elements.

      Pre-Condition:

      - VectorAdapter is initialized with 5 elements: ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5"]

      - SubListAdapter is created from indices 2 to 5 of the vector

      Post-Condition:

      - String representation is "[3, 4, 5]"

      - No changes to the sublist state

      Expected Results:

      A sublist starting at index 2 of ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5"] should have the string representation "[3, 4, 5]".
